report.source_text: Diagnostic paracentesis was performed with the resulting fluid biochemistry as follows: lactate dehydrogenase of 1255 U/L, total protein of 53 g/L, pH 7.76 and alkaline phosphatase of 51 U/L. Fluid cytology showed neoplastic cells with moderate amount of eosinophilic cytoplasm and rare papillary-like structures. Immunochemistry staining showed PAX8-positive, CD10-positive and CK7-positive cells consistent with carcinoma of renal origin (figure 3). There was no bacterial growth from the ascitic fluid culture.

report.source_text: He was subsequently reviewed by the Medical Oncology team, which commenced on 20 mg daily dose of cabozantinib, a small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor. He initially reported good improvement in his abdominal pain symptoms within 1 month of therapy commencement. This improvement was further supported by a repeat staging CT of the brain, chest, abdomen and pelvis, showing stable peritoneal and pulmonary nodules and resolution of ascites and pleural effusion. There was no evidence of other metastatic foci on CT and whole-body bone scan.

clinician.final_diagnosis: pT2 Nx type 1 papillary renal cell carcinoma (pRCC)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old man with a history of laparoscopic left radical nephrectomy for an 80 mm Bosniak IV cystic renal mass presented 5 months later with worsening abdominal pain, distension, and loss of appetite. Histopathology of the nephrectomy specimen confirmed pT2 Nx type 1 papillary renal cell carcinoma, nuclear grade 2, with negative margins and no lymphovascular invasion (E003). Imaging at presentation revealed moderate-volume ascites, peritoneal nodules, right pleural effusion, and a right apical subpleural nodule without locoregional recurrence (E004). Diagnostic paracentesis showed fluid lactate dehydrogenase of 1255 U/L and protein of 53 g/L, with cytology confirming neoplastic cells positive for PAX8, CD10, and CK7 consistent with renal carcinoma metastasis (E005). Treatment with cabozantinib led to symptomatic improvement and imaging after one month demonstrated stable nodules and resolution of ascites and pleural effusion with no new metastatic sites (E006).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Histopathology confirmed pT2 Nx type 1 papillary renal cell carcinoma with negative margins and no lymphovascular invasion
Imaging showed ascites, peritoneal nodules, pleural effusion, and no local recurrence
Paracentesis cytology demonstrated renal carcinoma metastatic cells positive for PAX8, CD10, and CK7
Cabozantinib treatment resulted in symptom improvement and resolution of ascites and pleural effusion on follow-up imaging

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Imaging showed no locoregional recurrence in the left renal bed
